name: Anguish-Pyralis
geological_features: Obsidian spire fields rising from cooling lava seas
Continent-wide fissure networks venting superheated gas
specific_features: Distress beacon of unknown origin broadcasting from within an active lava tube
description: Anguish-Pyralis is a small volcanic world whose surface is a hellscape of cooling lava seas punctuated by forests of obsidian spires that shatter and reform in endless cycles of creation and destruction. The fissure networks that web the continents exhale superheated gas in screaming jets that can be heard through the hull of an orbiting vessel.

The toxic atmosphere is a sulphurous shroud that obscures the surface in perpetual murk, lit from below by the orange glow of exposed magma. The planet seems to exist in a state of ongoing torment, its geology contorted into shapes that evoke suffering in a way that unsettles even veteran surveyors.

A distress beacon broadcasts continuously from within an active lava tube system near the equator, its signal pattern matching no known standard. The beacon has been active for at least two hundred years based on signal degradation analysis, yet it continues to function in an environment that should have destroyed any known technology within hours.

No life has been detected on the surface, and the planet's resources, while present, are accessible only through extreme engineering measures. Anguish-Pyralis's primary significance is the mystery of the beacon: who placed it, what technology sustains it, and whether it represents a call for help or a warning to stay away.
